title: Folding a fitted sheet
hook: Corners tucked into each other, or folded apart. Does it change the fold?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: that tucking one elastic corner inside another lets the corners share the same space, so the folded sheet lies flatter

misconception: A fitted sheet can't be folded flat; its elastic corners always leave a lump.
objective: Each elastic corner is a cup of cloth. Kept apart, four cups stack as four full depths. Tucked inside one another, they share one hollow, and each extra corner adds only a thin layer of cloth.

recall.question: A corner pocket is 8 cm tall on its own, and each extra corner nested inside adds 2 cm. How tall are 4 corners nested, against 4 kept separate?
recall.why: Nesting shares the hollow: 8 + 3 × 2 = 14 cm. Kept separate, each pocket needs its own 8 cm: 4 × 8 = 32 cm. No material was removed. Real elastic and seams change the numbers.
